1	# SMA-745 — release-plz `POST /git/refs` 403 after a workflow-changing merge
2	
3	Linear: [SMA-745](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-745). Branch:
4	`feature/sma-745-release-plz-post-gitrefs-returns-403-when-a-workflow`.
5	
6	## Intent
7	
8	A `release-plz` run must not leave a crate published on crates.io without its
9	git tag and GitHub release. Sven said that the result to avoid is "a release that
10	one must repair by hand". A larger permission for the paigasusbot App is
11	acceptable to get this, but the extra risk that it brings must be contained in
12	the same change.
13	
14	If a release still leaves a gap for a different cause, the `release-plz` run
15	must report the gap and be red. Nobody must find it later by accident.
16	
17	## What happened
18	
19	On 2026-10-30, two `release-plz.yml` runs failed with `403 Forbidden` and an
20	empty body on `POST /repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/refs`:
21	
22	| Run | Commit | Failed call | Effect |
23	| -- | -- | -- | -- |
24	| 41119756553 | `91a6ae65` (PR 314) | create branch `release-plz-2026-10-30T20-04-51Z` | none; the next run opened the release PR |
25	| 41137079475 | `edc06f74` (PR 317) | create tag `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17` | evals 0.1.17 is on crates.io with **no tag and no GitHub release** |
26	
27	In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` (PR 315, PR 318) merged
28	while the run was in progress.
29	
30	## Cause (tested on 2026-10-31)
31	
32	GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes
33	on `main`, unless the token has the `workflow` permission. We tested this with
34	Sven's `gh` OAuth token (scopes `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`; no `workflow`):
35	
36	| Target commit | Position | Result |
37	| -- | -- | -- |
38	| `edc06f74` | behind `main` by PR 318 (workflow change) | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
39	| `b69fbf13` | tip of `main` | ref created (deleted again immediately) |
40	
41	The token, the ref name (`refs/heads/release-plz-sma745-repro`) and the call
42	were the same. Only the commit was different. An OAuth token gets 404 and the App
43	token got 403. Both are refusals of the same check.
44	
45	Not tested: that an App token **with** `workflows: write` succeeds. We cannot
46	make an App token locally (the private key is only in Actions secrets). The
47	first release-plz run with a workflow merge during the run is the first real
48	evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
49	
50	Other facts checked:
51	
52	- The permission covers every ref write by release-plz: the tag ref in
53	  `release`, and the branch create and force-update in `release-pr`. A GitHub
54	  release on an existing tag, a tag object, and a commit made through the API
55	  create no ref.
56	- Token expiry (1 hour) is not a second cause. The longest of the last 30
57	  release-plz runs took 12 minutes.
58	- release-plz makes **annotated** tags (for example, the ref for
59	  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.16` points to an object of type `tag`). It makes
60	  the tag object first, then the ref. In run 41137079475 the tag object
61	  `93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a` was made (tag
62	  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17`, object `edc06f74…`, tagger
63	  `paigasusbot[bot]`); only the ref failed.
64	- `release-plz.toml` sets no `git_tag_name`, so the tag format is the default
65	  `<package>-v<version>`.
66	
67	## Goals
68	
69	1. The paigasusbot installation token can create refs behind workflow changes.
70	2. The extra power of that token cannot reach the release secrets from a
71	   branch other than `main`.
72	3. Each `release-plz` run checks for published versions without a tag or a
73	   GitHub release, reports each gap with recovery commands, and is red when a
74	   gap exists.
75	4. The runbook describes this failure, the evidence, the report and the
76	   recovery.
77	5. `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 gets its tag and its GitHub release.
78	
79	## Non-goals
80	
81	- Automatic repair of a gap. The report only reports.
82	- A change to the `concurrency` group. The runs did not overlap; it works.
83	- Rules about the merge order of PRs, except during the rollout of this PR.
84	- A check of older versions. Only the version at the run's commit is checked.
85	
86	## Anti-goals
87	
88	- A gap report that says "no gaps" when it could not check. A network error, an
89	  API error, an empty package list or an unexpected response must show as
90	  "could not check", never as success.
91	- A report step that hides the original failure. The job stays red when
92	  release-plz failed.
93	- A gap report that gives wrong recovery commands because an auth or rate-limit
94	  error looked like "missing".
95	
96	## Constraints
97	
98	- Sven added `Workflows: Read and write` to the paigasusbot App (ID 3742291) on
99	  2026-10-31, and confirmed that the installation on `SMK1085/paigasus-helikon`
100	  accepted it.
101	- No PR runs `release-plz.yml`. The first real test of the workflow change is
102	  the first push to `main` after the merge. Static guards and a self-test in the
103	  required `fmt` job protect what can be checked before that.
104	- crates.io rejects the default curl User-Agent with 403. Every crates.io
105	  request sets a custom User-Agent. The crates.io crawler policy asks for a
106	  maximum of 1 request per second.
107	- Release infrastructure commits use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)`, never
108	  `feat`/`fix`. The scope `workflows` is valid in `.versionrc` and in the
109	  `pr-title.yml` allowlist on `main`. PR title:
110	  `chore(workflows): SMA-745 <lowercase subject>`.
111	- This PR changes no packaged crate file, so release-plz makes no version bump
112	  for it.
113	- Actions stay SHA-pinned. This change adds no new action.
114	
115	## Design
116	
117	### 1. Token permission (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`)
118	
119	Add `permission-workflows: write` to the `actions/create-github-app-token`
120	step, next to `permission-contents` and `permission-pull-requests`. Add a short
121	comment: refs at a commit behind a workflow change need it (SMA-745).
122	
123	The workflow-level `permissions:` block is for `GITHUB_TOKEN` and stays as it
124	is.
125	
126	### 2. Release secrets in a `release` environment (Sven's decision)
127	
128	Risk: App 3742291 is a bypass actor on the `branch-names` ruleset. With
129	`contents: write` and `workflows: write`, a leaked installation token can push a
130	branch that contains a new `on: push` workflow. Today, that workflow can read
131	every repository secret, including `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and
132	`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`. The token is in the env of the release-plz step, so a
133	build script that runs during `cargo publish --verify` can probably read it.
134	
135	Mitigation:
136	
137	- A GitHub environment `release` with a deployment branch policy that allows
138	  only the `main` branch (custom branch policy, one entry: `main`). No required
139	  reviewers, because the release must stay automatic.
140	- The three secrets `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`
141	  and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` move from repository secrets to environment
142	  secrets of `release`. They are used only in `release-plz.yml`.
143	- The `release-plz` job sets `environment: release`.
144	- The environment and its branch policy are configuration as code: extend
145	  `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` to create or update the environment
146	  idempotently. Document it where `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes "Repo
147	  configuration".
148	- A workflow on another branch then cannot read these secrets. The job on `main`
149	  reads the environment secrets, which override repository secrets of the same
150	  name.
151	
152	Secret values cannot be read back from GitHub, so Sven sets the environment
153	secrets by hand. Recommended: use the move to rotate. Make a new App private key
154	and a new crates.io token (publish-update scope), set them on the environment,
155	and revoke the old ones after the first good run.
156	
157	### 3. Gap report on each run
158	
159	A new script `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`, and a new last step in
160	`release-plz.yml`:
161	
162	```yaml
163	- name: report release gaps
164	  if: ${{ always() && (steps.release.outcome == 'success' || steps.release.outcome == 'failure' || steps.release.outcome == 'cancelled') }}
165	  timeout-minutes: 5
166	  env:
167	    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
168	    RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.release.outcome }}
169	  run: bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh
170	```
171	
172	The `release` command step gets `id: release`. The report runs when the release
173	step ran (success, failure or cancelled). It does not run when the release step
174	was skipped, because then nothing was published. (Builder: a job-level
175	cancellation can stop `always()` steps too; this is accepted.)
176	
177	The report uses `github.token`, not the App token. The App token can be the
178	cause of the failure, and it can be expired. The workflow-level
179	`contents: write` gives read access to refs and releases, and `github.token`
180	is valid for the whole job.
181	
182	**Package list.** The script reads the versions **before** release-plz runs, so
183	that `release-pr` cannot change what it reads: a step before the release step
184	writes `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` to a file, and the script
185	reads it from a path in an env var (`RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA`). If the env var is
186	not set (local use), the script runs `cargo metadata` itself. It keeps the
187	packages whose `publish` field is not `[]`. If the list is empty, or the
188	metadata cannot be read or parsed, the result is "could not check".
189	
190	**Tag format guard.** If `release-plz.toml` contains `git_tag_name`,
191	`git_tag_enable` or `git_release_enable`, the result is "could not check" with a

194	
195	**Per package**, with a 1-second pause between crates.io requests and a time
196	limit on every call (`curl --max-time 20`, `timeout 30` around `gh`):
197	
198	- crates.io: `GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>` with a custom
199	  User-Agent. Require 200 and read `versions[].num`. The version is in the list
200	  → published. Not in the list → not published, no gap. A 404 for the crate
201	  itself → "could not check" (every publishable crate here is already on
202	  crates.io; a 404 more probably means a wrong URL or an API change). Any other
203	  result → "could not check".
204	- tag: `GET /repos/{repo}/git/ref/tags/<name>-v<version>` (singular `ref`,
205	  exact match, not a prefix match). 200 → present. 404 → missing. Any other
206	  status → "could not check".
207	- release: `GET /repos/{repo}/releases/tags/<name>-v<version>`. 200 and not a
208	  draft → present. 200 and a draft, or 404 → missing. Any other status →

210	
211	The script reads HTTP status codes explicitly (for example `gh api --include`
212	or `curl -w '%{http_code}'`). A non-zero exit of `gh` alone is never read as

214

# SMA-745 — release-plz `POST /git/refs` 403 after a workflow-changing merge

Linear: [SMA-745](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-745). Branch:
`feature/sma-745-release-plz-post-gitrefs-returns-403-when-a-workflow`.

## Intent

A `release-plz` run must not leave a crate published on crates.io without its
git tag and GitHub release. Sven said that the result to avoid is "a release that
one must repair by hand". A larger permission for the paigasusbot App is
acceptable to get this, but the extra risk that it brings must be contained in
the same change.

If a release still leaves a gap for a different cause, the `release-plz` run
must report the gap and be red. Nobody must find it later by accident.

## What happened

On 2026-10-30, two `release-plz.yml` runs failed with `403 Forbidden` and an
empty body on `POST /repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/refs`:

| Run | Commit | Failed call | Effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 41119756553 | `91a6ae65` (PR 314) | create branch `release-plz-2026-10-30T20-04-51Z` | none; the next run opened the release PR |
| 41137079475 | `edc06f74` (PR 317) | create tag `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17` | evals 0.1.17 is on crates.io with **no tag and no GitHub release** |

In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` (PR 315, PR 318) merged
while the run was in progress.

## Cause (tested on 2026-10-31)

GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes
on `main`, unless the token has the `workflow` permission. We tested this with
Sven's `gh` OAuth token (scopes `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`; no `workflow`):

| Target commit | Position | Result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `edc06f74` | behind `main` by PR 318 (workflow change) | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
| `b69fbf13` | tip of `main` | ref created (deleted again immediately) |

The token, the ref name (`refs/heads/release-plz-sma745-repro`) and the call
were the same. Only the commit was different. An OAuth token gets 404 and the App
token got 403. Both are refusals of the same check.

Not tested: that an App token **with** `workflows: write` succeeds. We cannot
make an App token locally (the private key is only in Actions secrets). The
first release-plz run with a workflow merge during the run is the first real
evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.

Other facts checked:

- The permission covers every ref write by release-plz: the tag ref in
  `release`, and the branch create and force-update in `release-pr`. A GitHub
  release on an existing tag, a tag object, and a commit made through the API
  create no ref.
- Token expiry (1 hour) is not a second cause. The longest of the last 30
  release-plz runs took 12 minutes.
- release-plz makes **annotated** tags (for example, the ref for
  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.16` points to an object of type `tag`). It makes
  the tag object first, then the ref. In run 41137079475 the tag object
  `93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a` was made (tag
  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17`, object `edc06f74…`, tagger
  `paigasusbot[bot]`); only the ref failed.
- `release-plz.toml` sets no `git_tag_name`, so the tag format is the default
  `<package>-v<version>`.

## Goals

1. The paigasusbot installation token can create refs behind workflow changes.
2. The extra power of that token cannot reach the release secrets from a
   branch other than `main`.
3. Each `release-plz` run checks for published versions without a tag or a
   GitHub release, reports each gap with recovery commands, and is red when a
   gap exists.
4. The runbook describes this failure, the evidence, the report and the
   recovery.
5. `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 gets its tag and its GitHub release.

## Non-goals

- Automatic repair of a gap. The report only reports.
- A change to the `concurrency` group. The runs did not overlap; it works.
- Rules about the merge order of PRs, except during the rollout of this PR.
- A check of older versions. Only the version at the run's commit is checked.

## Anti-goals

- A gap report that says "no gaps" when it could not check. A network error, an
  API error, an empty package list or an unexpected response must show as
  "could not check", never as success.
- A report step that hides the original failure. The job stays red when
  release-plz failed.
- A gap report that gives wrong recovery commands because an auth or rate-limit
  error looked like "missing".

## Constraints

- Sven added `Workflows: Read and write` to the paigasusbot App (ID 3742291) on
  2026-10-31, and confirmed that the installation on `SMK1085/paigasus-helikon`
  accepted it.
- No PR runs `release-plz.yml`. The first real test of the workflow change is
  the first push to `main` after the merge. Static guards and a self-test in the
  required `fmt` job protect what can be checked before that.
- crates.io rejects the default curl User-Agent with 403. Every crates.io
  request sets a custom User-Agent. The crates.io crawler policy asks for a
  maximum of 1 request per second.
- Release infrastructure commits use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)`, never
  `feat`/`fix`. The scope `workflows` is valid in `.versionrc` and in the
  `pr-title.yml` allowlist on `main`. PR title:
  `chore(workflows): SMA-745 <lowercase subject>`.
- This PR changes no packaged crate file, so release-plz makes no version bump
  for it.
- Actions stay SHA-pinned. This change adds no new action.

## Design

### 1. Token permission (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`)

Add `permission-workflows: write` to the `actions/create-github-app-token`
step, next to `permission-contents` and `permission-pull-requests`. Add a short
comment: refs at a commit behind a workflow change need it (SMA-745).

The workflow-level `permissions:` block is for `GITHUB_TOKEN` and stays as it
is.

### 2. Release secrets in a `release` environment (Sven's decision)

Risk: App 3742291 is a bypass actor on the `branch-names` ruleset. With
`contents: write` and `workflows: write`, a leaked installation token can push a
branch that contains a new `on: push` workflow. Today, that workflow can read
every repository secret, including `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and
`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`. The token is in the env of the release-plz step, so a
build script that runs during `cargo publish --verify` can probably read it.

Mitigation:

- A GitHub environment `release` with a deployment branch policy that allows
  only the `main` branch (custom branch policy, one entry: `main`). No required
  reviewers, because the release must stay automatic.
- The three secrets `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`
  and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` move from repository secrets to environment
  secrets of `release`. They are used only in `release-plz.yml`.
- The `release-plz` job sets `environment: release`.
- The environment and its branch policy are configuration as code: extend
  `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` to create or update the environment
  idempotently. Document it where `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes "Repo
  configuration".
- A workflow on another branch then cannot read these secrets. The job on `main`
  reads the environment secrets, which override repository secrets of the same
  name.

Secret values cannot be read back from GitHub, so Sven sets the environment
secrets by hand. Recommended: use the move to rotate. Make a new App private key
and a new crates.io token (publish-update scope), set them on the environment,
and revoke the old ones after the first good run.

### 3. Gap report on each run

A new script `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`, and a new last step in
`release-plz.yml`:

```yaml
- name: report release gaps
  if: ${{ always() && (steps.release.outcome == 'success' || steps.release.outcome == 'failure' || steps.release.outcome == 'cancelled') }}
  timeout-minutes: 5
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.release.outcome }}
  run: bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh
```

The `release` command step gets `id: release`. The report runs when the release
step ran (success, failure or cancelled). It does not run when the release step
was skipped, because then nothing was published. (Builder: a job-level
cancellation can stop `always()` steps too; this is accepted.)

The report uses `github.token`, not the App token. The App token can be the
cause of the failure, and it can be expired. The workflow-level
`contents: write` gives read access to refs and releases, and `github.token`
is valid for the whole job.

**Package list.** The script reads the versions **before** release-plz runs, so
that `release-pr` cannot change what it reads: a step before the release step
writes `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` to a file, and the script
reads it from a path in an env var (`RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA`). If the env var is
not set (local use), the script runs `cargo metadata` itself. It keeps the
packages whose `publish` field is not `[]`. If the list is empty, or the
metadata cannot be read or parsed, the result is "could not check".

**Tag format guard.** If `release-plz.toml` contains `git_tag_name`,
`git_tag_enable` or `git_release_enable`, the result is "could not check" with a
clear message. The script assumes `<package>-v<version>` and must not guess
another format.

**Per package**, with a 1-second pause between crates.io requests and a time
limit on every call (`curl --max-time 20`, `timeout 30` around `gh`):

- crates.io: `GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>` with a custom
  User-Agent. Require 200 and read `versions[].num`. The version is in the list
  → published. Not in the list → not published, no gap. A 404 for the crate
  itself → "could not check" (every publishable crate here is already on
  crates.io; a 404 more probably means a wrong URL or an API change). Any other
  result → "could not check".
- tag: `GET /repos/{repo}/git/ref/tags/<name>-v<version>` (singular `ref`,
  exact match, not a prefix match). 200 → present. 404 → missing. Any other
  status → "could not check".
- release: `GET /repos/{repo}/releases/tags/<name>-v<version>`. 200 and not a
  draft → present. 200 and a draft, or 404 → missing. Any other status →
  "could not check".

The script reads HTTP status codes explicitly (for example `gh api --include`
or `curl -w '%{http_code}'`). A non-zero exit of `gh` alone is never read as
"missing".

**Output.**

- For each gap: a line in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (when set) with the crate, the
  version, what is missing, and the recovery commands. Without
  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (local use), the same text goes to stdout.
- One summary `::error::` annotation for all gaps (GitHub shows a maximum of 10
  annotations per step, and multi-line messages need `%0A`).
- Each "could not check" item is listed with its reason.

**Recovery text** for a missing tag: first look for the tag object from the
failed run in the run log; if none is known, make a new annotated tag that
points at the run commit (`$GITHUB_SHA` in CI, `HEAD` locally). Then create the
ref. For a missing release: `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag
--latest=false` with the version's CHANGELOG section as notes. The text states
that the token needs the `workflow` scope.

**Exit codes and job result.**

| Result | Exit code | On a red release step | On a green release step |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| no gaps | 0 | job stays red (release failed) | green |
| at least one gap (with or without "could not check") | 1 | red | **red** |
| "could not check", no gap | 2 | red | `::warning::`, step exits 0 |

The script gets the release-step outcome from `RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME`. Only the
"could not check on a green run" case changes the exit code; the script maps 2
to a warning and exit 0 there. A green run with a gap is red, because a gap is a
broken release.

Locally: `GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`. Before
the evals recovery, it must report exactly one gap:
`paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17, tag and release missing.

### 4. Self-test and static guards in CI

The report runs on each release-plz run, but only on `main`. Add
`scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh`. It runs the script with fake `curl`
and `gh` commands on `PATH` and a fixture metadata JSON through
`RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA` (no live cargo, network or GitHub). It checks the exit
code **and** the output text (crate name, version, "could not check" reason).
Cases:

- all versions tagged and released → 0
- published, no tag → 1, crate and version in the output
- published, tag present, no release → 1
- published, release is a draft → 1
- version not in the crates.io list → 0
- crates.io returns 404 for the crate → 2
- crates.io returns 500, or no response → 2
- crates.io returns 429 → 2
- tag call returns 500 → 2; release call returns 401 → 2
- one gap plus one "could not check" → 1, both shown
- only a longer tag with the same prefix exists (`…-v0.1.17` vs
  `…-v0.1.170`) → 1
- metadata cannot be read → 2; zero publishable packages → 2
- `release-plz.toml` with `git_tag_name` → 2
- `RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME=success` and "could not check" only → 0 with a warning

Static guards in the same self-test (no PR runs `release-plz.yml`, so these are
the only pre-merge protection for it): `release-plz.yml` contains
`permission-workflows: write`, `environment: release`, `id: release`, and a step
that runs `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`.

Run the self-test as a step in the `fmt` job of `ci.yml`, next to
`check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh`. `fmt` is a required check.

Add the new self-test command to the lists of local CI gates in `CLAUDE.md`
("To reproduce every CI gate locally") and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and to the `fmt`
job description in `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

### 5. Runbook (`docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`)

Add a section "A red release-plz run with 403 on `git/refs` (SMA-745)":

- the cause and the test evidence (short form of "Cause" above)
- the fix (the `workflows` permission) and what to do if the installation loses
  it (the token step fails)
- the `release` environment: what it protects, and that secrets are set there,
  not as repository secrets
- how to read the gap report and its three results
- the recovery commands
- the general rule: a red release-plz run can still have published crates; read
  the gap report, do not assume that nothing shipped.

The section is in the markdown-lint gate.

### 6. Rollout (order matters)

1. Done: the App has `Workflows: Read and write`, and the installation accepted
   it.
2. Before the merge: Sven runs `sh scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` from this
   branch (creates the `release` environment with the `main`-only branch
   policy) and sets the three environment secrets (new values recommended).
3. Merge only when no `release-plz` run is queued or in progress. This PR
   changes workflow files, so a run in progress at merge time can hit the
   SMA-745 failure one more time.
4. After the merge, read the first run: the token step succeeds, the job shows
   a deployment to `release`, and the gap report runs. The evals 0.1.17 gap may
   still show if step 7 is not done yet; that is expected and correct.
5. Delete the three repository-level secrets. Revoke the old App private key and
   the old crates.io token if new ones were made.
6. Rollback: revert the workflow change. The App permission and the
   environment can stay. Before a rollback, the repository-level secrets must
   exist again.
7. evals 0.1.17 recovery (Sven runs it, see below). It does not depend on the
   merge.

### 7. Recovery of evals 0.1.17 (Sven runs it)

The auto-mode classifier blocks ref creation by the agent, and Sven's token needs
the `workflow` scope first. The builder extracts the 0.1.17 section of
`crates/paigasus-helikon-evals/CHANGELOG.md` to a file and gives Sven these
commands with the real path:

```bash
gh auth refresh -s workflow
# Check that the tag object still exists and is the right one:
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/tags/93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a \
  --jq '{tag, sha: .object.sha}'
# expect: tag paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17, sha edc06f74bcf537d6c7a49ea60e696d3b45c4dfa7
gh api -X POST repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/refs \
  -f ref=refs/tags/paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17 \
  -f sha=93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a
gh release create paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17 --verify-tag --latest=false \
  --title paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17 --notes-file <path>
gh auth refresh -r workflow
```

If the ref call returns 422 (GitHub removed the unreferenced tag object), the
fallback is a new annotated tag object at `edc06f74…` through
`POST /git/tags`, then the ref. After the recovery, the local gap report must
say "no gaps".

## Decisions and who made them

- **The fix is the permission** — Sven chose this direction ("a release that one
  must repair by hand" is the result to avoid) and added the permission.
- **Move the release secrets into a `main`-only environment, in this PR** —
  Sven, after the challenge showed the security cost.
- **Report on every run, red on a gap also when release-plz is green** — Sven
  first said "a red run of release-plz should report it", then agreed to run it
  on every run.
- **Report only, no auto-repair** — my call. An automatic repair needs the same
  permission, so it adds no protection against this cause.
- **Only the current version per crate** — my call. release-plz publishes the
  version at the run's commit.
- **The report uses `github.token`** — my call, from the challenge.
- **Versions read before release-plz runs** — my call, so that `release-pr`
  cannot change them.
- **No mdBook or crate README edits** — conscious call. This is release plumbing,
  not a user-facing change.

## Left to the builder

1	# SMA-745 — release-plz `POST /git/refs` 403 after a workflow-changing merge
2	
3	Linear: [SMA-745](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-745). Branch:
4	`feature/sma-745-release-plz-post-gitrefs-returns-403-when-a-workflow`.
5	
6	## Intent
7	
8	A `release-plz` run must not leave a crate published on crates.io without its
9	git tag and GitHub release. Sven said that the result to avoid is "a release that
10	one must repair by hand". A larger permission for the paigasusbot App is
11	acceptable to get this, but the extra risk that it brings must be contained in
12	the same change.
13	
14	If a release still leaves a gap for a different cause, the `release-plz` run
15	must report the gap and be red. Nobody must find it later by accident.
16	
17	## What happened
18	
19	On 2026-10-30, two `release-plz.yml` runs failed with `403 Forbidden` and an
20	empty body on `POST /repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/refs`:
21	
22	| Run | Commit | Failed call | Effect |
23	| -- | -- | -- | -- |
24	| 41119756553 | `91a6ae65` (PR 314) | create branch `release-plz-2026-10-30T20-04-51Z` | none; the next run opened the release PR |
25	| 41137079475 | `edc06f74` (PR 317) | create tag `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17` | evals 0.1.17 is on crates.io with **no tag and no GitHub release** |
26	
27	In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` (PR 315, PR 318) merged
28	while the run was in progress.
29	
30	## Cause (tested on 2026-10-31)
31	
32	GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes
33	on `main`, unless the token has the `workflow` permission. We tested this with
34	Sven's `gh` OAuth token (scopes `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`; no `workflow`):
35	
36	| Target commit | Position | Result |
37	| -- | -- | -- |
38	| `edc06f74` | behind `main` by PR 318 (workflow change) | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
39	| `b69fbf13` | tip of `main` | ref created (deleted again immediately) |
40	
41	The token, the ref name (`refs/heads/release-plz-sma745-repro`) and the call
42	were the same. Only the commit was different. An OAuth token gets 404 and the App
43	token got 403. Both are refusals of the same check.
44	
45	Not tested: that an App token **with** `workflows: write` succeeds. We cannot
46	make an App token locally (the private key is only in Actions secrets). The
47	first release-plz run with a workflow merge during the run is the first real
48	evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
49	
50	Other facts checked:
51	
52	- The permission covers every ref write by release-plz: the tag ref in
53	  `release`, and the branch create and force-update in `release-pr`. A GitHub
54	  release on an existing tag, a tag object, and a commit made through the API
55	  create no ref.
56	- Token expiry (1 hour) is not a second cause. The longest of the last 30
57	  release-plz runs took 12 minutes.
58	- release-plz makes **annotated** tags (for example, the ref for
59	  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.16` points to an object of type `tag`). It makes
60	  the tag object first, then the ref. In run 41137079475 the tag object
61	  `93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a` was made (tag
62	  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17`, object `edc06f74…`, tagger
63	  `paigasusbot[bot]`); only the ref failed.
64	- `release-plz.toml` sets no `git_tag_name`, so the tag format is the default
65	  `<package>-v<version>`.
66	
67	## Goals
68	
69	1. The paigasusbot installation token can create refs behind workflow changes.
70	2. The extra power of that token cannot reach the release secrets from a
71	   branch other than `main`.
72	3. Each `release-plz` run checks for published versions without a tag or a
73	   GitHub release, reports each gap with recovery commands, and is red when a
74	   gap exists.
75	4. The runbook describes this failure, the evidence, the report and the
76	   recovery.
77	5. `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 gets its tag and its GitHub release.
78	
79	## Non-goals
80	
81	- Automatic repair of a gap. The report only reports.
82	- A change to the `concurrency` group. The runs did not overlap; it works.
83	- Rules about the merge order of PRs, except during the rollout of this PR.
84	- A check of older versions. Only the version at the run's commit is checked.
85	
86	## Anti-goals
87	
88	- A gap report that says "no gaps" when it could not check. A network error, an
89	  API error, an empty package list or an unexpected response must show as
90	  "could not check", never as success.
91	- A report step that hides the original failure. The job stays red when
92	  release-plz failed.
93	- A gap report that gives wrong recovery commands because an auth or rate-limit
94	  error looked like "missing".
95	
96	## Constraints
97	
98	- Sven added `Workflows: Read and write` to the paigasusbot App (ID 3742291) on
99	  2026-10-31, and confirmed that the installation on `SMK1085/paigasus-helikon`
100	  accepted it.
101	- No PR runs `release-plz.yml`. The first real test of the workflow change is
102	  the first push to `main` after the merge. Static guards and a self-test in the
103	  required `fmt` job protect what can be checked before that.
104	- crates.io rejects the default curl User-Agent with 403. Every crates.io
105	  request sets a custom User-Agent. The crates.io crawler policy asks for a
106	  maximum of 1 request per second.
107	- Release infrastructure commits use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)`, never
108	  `feat`/`fix`. The scope `workflows` is valid in `.versionrc` and in the
109	  `pr-title.yml` allowlist on `main`. PR title:
110	  `chore(workflows): SMA-745 <lowercase subject>`.
111	- This PR changes no packaged crate file, so release-plz makes no version bump
112	  for it.
113	- Actions stay SHA-pinned. This change adds no new action.
114	
115	## Design
116	
117	### 1. Token permission (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`)
118	
119	Add `permission-workflows: write` to the `actions/create-github-app-token`
120	step, next to `permission-contents` and `permission-pull-requests`. Add a short
121	comment: refs at a commit behind a workflow change need it (SMA-745).
122	
123	The workflow-level `permissions:` block is for `GITHUB_TOKEN` and stays as it
124	is.
125	
126	### 2. Release secrets in a `release` environment (Sven's decision)
127	
128	Risk: App 3742291 is a bypass actor on the `branch-names` ruleset. With
129	`contents: write` and `workflows: write`, a leaked installation token can push a
130	branch that contains a new `on: push` workflow. Today, that workflow can read
131	every repository secret, including `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and
132	`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`. The token is in the env of the release-plz step, so a
133	build script that runs during `cargo publish --verify` can probably read it.
134	
135	Mitigation:
136	
137	- A GitHub environment `release` with a deployment branch policy that allows
138	  only the `main` branch (custom branch policy, one entry: `main`). No required
139	  reviewers, because the release must stay automatic.
140	- The three secrets `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`
141	  and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` move from repository secrets to environment
142	  secrets of `release`. They are used only in `release-plz.yml`.
143	- The `release-plz` job sets `environment: release`.
144	- The environment and its branch policy are configuration as code: extend
145	  `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` to create or update the environment
146	  idempotently. Document it where `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes "Repo
147	  configuration".
148	- A workflow on another branch then cannot read these secrets. The job on `main`
149	  reads the environment secrets, which override repository secrets of the same
150	  name.
151	
152	Secret values cannot be read back from GitHub, so Sven sets the environment
153	secrets by hand. Recommended: use the move to rotate. Make a new App private key
154	and a new crates.io token (publish-update scope), set them on the environment,
155	and revoke the old ones after the first good run.
156	
157	### 3. Gap report on each run
158	
159	A new script `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`, and a new last step in
160	`release-plz.yml`:
161	
162	```yaml
163	- name: report release gaps
164	  if: ${{ always() && (steps.release.outcome == 'success' || steps.release.outcome == 'failure' || steps.release.outcome == 'cancelled') }}
165	  timeout-minutes: 5
166	  env:
167	    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
168	    RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.release.outcome }}
169	  run: bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh
170	```
171	
172	The `release` command step gets `id: release`. The report runs when the release
173	step ran (success, failure or cancelled). It does not run when the release step
174	was skipped, because then nothing was published. (Builder: a job-level
175	cancellation can stop `always()` steps too; this is accepted.)
176	
177	The report uses `github.token`, not the App token. The App token can be the
178	cause of the failure, and it can be expired. The workflow-level
179	`contents: write` gives read access to refs and releases, and `github.token`
180	is valid for the whole job.
181	
182	**Package list.** The script reads the versions **before** release-plz runs, so
183	that `release-pr` cannot change what it reads: a step before the release step
184	writes `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` to a file, and the script
185	reads it from a path in an env var (`RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA`). If the env var is
186	not set (local use), the script runs `cargo metadata` itself. It keeps the
187	packages whose `publish` field is not `[]`. If the list is empty, or the
188	metadata cannot be read or parsed, the result is "could not check".
189	
190	**Tag format guard.** If `release-plz.toml` contains `git_tag_name`,
191	`git_tag_enable` or `git_release_enable`, the result is "could not check" with a
192	clear message. The script assumes `<package>-v<version>` and must not guess
193	another format.
194	
195	**Per package**, with a 1-second pause between crates.io requests and a time
196	limit on every call (`curl --max-time 20`, `timeout 30` around `gh`):
197	
198	- crates.io: `GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<name>` with a custom
199	  User-Agent. Require 200 and read `versions[].num`. The version is in the list
200	  → published. Not in the list → not published, no gap. A 404 for the crate
201	  itself → "could not check" (every publishable crate here is already on
202	  crates.io; a 404 more probably means a wrong URL or an API change). Any other
203	  result → "could not check".
204	- tag: `GET /repos/{repo}/git/ref/tags/<name>-v<version>` (singular `ref`,
205	  exact match, not a prefix match). 200 → present. 404 → missing. Any other
206	  status → "could not check".
207	- release: `GET /repos/{repo}/releases/tags/<name>-v<version>`. 200 and not a
208	  draft → present. 200 and a draft, or 404 → missing. Any other status →
209	  "could not check".
210	
211	The script reads HTTP status codes explicitly (for example `gh api --include`
212	or `curl -w '%{http_code}'`). A non-zero exit of `gh` alone is never read as
213	"missing".
214	
215	**Output.**
216	
217	- For each gap: a line in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (when set) with the crate, the
218	  version, what is missing, and the recovery commands. Without
219	  `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (local use), the same text goes to stdout.
220	- One summary `::error::` annotation for all gaps (GitHub shows a maximum of 10
221	  annotations per step, and multi-line messages need `%0A`).
222	- Each "could not check" item is listed with its reason.
223	
224	**Recovery text** for a missing tag: first look for the tag object from the
225	failed run in the run log; if none is known, make a new annotated tag that
226	points at the run commit (`$GITHUB_SHA` in CI, `HEAD` locally). Then create the
227	ref. For a missing release: `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag
228	--latest=false` with the version's CHANGELOG section as notes. The text states
229	that the token needs the `workflow` scope.
230	
231	**Exit codes and job result.**
232	
233	| Result | Exit code | On a red release step | On a green release step |
234	| -- | -- | -- | -- |
235	| no gaps | 0 | job stays red (release failed) | green |
236	| at least one gap (with or without "could not check") | 1 | red | **red** |
237	| "could not check", no gap | 2 | red | `::warning::`, step exits 0 |
238	
239	The script gets the release-step outcome from `RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME`. Only the
240	"could not check on a green run" case changes the exit code; the script maps 2
241	to a warning and exit 0 there. A green run with a gap is red, because a gap is a
242	broken release.
243	
244	Locally: `GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`. Before
245	the evals recovery, it must report exactly one gap:
246	`paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17, tag and release missing.
247	
248	### 4. Self-test and static guards in CI
249	
250	The report runs on each release-plz run, but only on `main`. Add
251	`scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh`. It runs the script with fake `curl`
252	and `gh` commands on `PATH` and a fixture metadata JSON through
253	`RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA` (no live cargo, network or GitHub). It checks the exit
254	code **and** the output text (crate name, version, "could not check" reason).
255	Cases:
256	
257	- all versions tagged and released → 0
258	- published, no tag → 1, crate and version in the output
259	- published, tag present, no release → 1
260	- published, release is a draft → 1
261	- version not in the crates.io list → 0
262	- crates.io returns 404 for the crate → 2
263	- crates.io returns 500, or no response → 2
264	- crates.io returns 429 → 2
265	- tag call returns 500 → 2; release call returns 401 → 2
266	- one gap plus one "could not check" → 1, both shown
267	- only a longer tag with the same prefix exists (`…-v0.1.17` vs
268	  `…-v0.1.170`) → 1
269	- metadata cannot be read → 2; zero publishable packages → 2
270	- `release-plz.toml` with `git_tag_name` → 2
271	- `RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME=success` and "could not check" only → 0 with a warning
272	
273	Static guards in the same self-test (no PR runs `release-plz.yml`, so these are
274	the only pre-merge protection for it): `release-plz.yml` contains
275	`permission-workflows: write`, `environment: release`, `id: release`, and a step
276	that runs `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`.
277

290	 ## Caveat 1 — same-PR core API needs a core bump (SMA-321)
291	 
292	 **Caveat — when the ascending crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too** (a 5th step). `cargo publish --verify` builds the ascending crate's tarball against the **registry** core (the `path` is stripped at publish), so if crates.io `core` lacks the new API the publish fails with `failed to verify package tarball`, and release-plz's combined job (SMA-351) aborts before its release-PR step — a deadlock, since `core` never gets its auto bump (a squashed `feat(<ascending-crate>)` commit attributes nothing to `core`). Fix: in the same PR, also bump `paigasus-helikon-core` (patch for additive/non-breaking-behind-`#[non_exhaustive]`, e.g. `0.2.0` → `0.2.1`) and its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin + CHANGELOG. release-plz then publishes `core` first, then the ascending crate verifies against the fresh `core` (dependency-ordered publish). Diagnosed in SMA-321: PR #45's release failed against the stale `core` `0.2.0`; PR #46 (`chore(release)` bumping `core` to `0.2.1`) cleared it.
293	 
294	 ## Caveat 2 — the manual core bump defeats the facade cascade (SMA-346)
295	 
296	 **Second-order caveat — the manual core bump silently defeats `dependencies_update`, so the facade drifts.** `release-plz.toml` sets `dependencies_update = true`, which is *supposed* to cascade: when a sibling's version changes, release-plz bumps the facade's `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and gives the facade a patch bump. But that cascade only runs when **release-plz itself performs the sibling bump**. The same-PR manual bump above means the sibling version is already at target when the PR merges, so release-plz just publishes it and never runs the dependent-bump step — the facade (`paigasus-helikon`) is left untouched and stops tracking. Consequence: the facade stays at its old version with stale published dep reqs (e.g. after SMA-346, facade `0.2.0` still requested `paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio = ^0.0.0`, so the new runner-boundary surface was unreachable through the facade's `runtime-tokio` feature). **Fix: in any PR that uses the same-PR manual bump, ALSO bump the facade** (patch: `version` in `crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` + its `[workspace.dependencies]` self-pin + CHANGELOG) so it republishes with current sibling reqs. 298	+## A red release-plz run with 403 on `git/refs` (SMA-745)
299	+
300	+**Symptom.** A `release-plz.yml` run fails with `403 Forbidden` and an empty body on `POST /repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs`. The failed call can create a release branch or a tag. On 2026-10-30, two runs failed this way. One run published `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 to crates.io and then failed to create the tag. The crate had no tag and no GitHub release.
301	+
302	+**Cause.** GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes on `main`. The token needs the `workflow` permission for this. In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` merged while the run was in progress. We tested this on 2026-10-31 with a token that had no `workflow` scope. The same call, ref name and token gave different results:
303	+
304	+| Target commit | Position | Result |
305	+| -- | -- | -- |
306	+| A commit behind a workflow change on `main` | behind `main` | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
307	+| The tip of `main` | tip of `main` | ref created |
308	+
309	+We measured only the 404 with the OAuth token. The App token got 403 in the incident runs. We think that both are refusals of the same check. We did **not** test that an App token with `workflows: write` succeeds, because the App private key exists only in Actions secrets. The first `release-plz` run that overlaps a workflow merge is the first real evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
310	+
311	+**Fix.** The `actions/create-github-app-token` step in `release-plz.yml` requests `permission-workflows: write`. The paigasusbot App (ID 3742291) has `Workflows: Read and write`. If the installation loses this permission, the token step fails. Then restore the permission in the App settings and accept it on the installation.
312	+
313	+**The `release` environment.** The extra power of the token has a risk. A leaked token can push a branch that has a new `on: push` workflow. Such a workflow can read repository secrets. The `release-plz` job therefore sets `environment: release`. This environment allows only the `main` branch. It has no required reviewers, so the release stays automatic. `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` creates the environment. Set `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as **environment** secrets of `release`, by hand. Do not set them as repository secrets. A repository-level copy would be readable from any branch.
314	+
315	+**The gap report.** Each `release-plz` run ends with the step "report release gaps". It runs `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`. For each publishable crate, it checks the version at the run commit. It reports a gap when crates.io lists the version but the tag `<package>-v<version>` or the non-draft GitHub release is missing. The script only reports. It does not repair. The step has three results:
316	+
317	+| Result | Exit code | Meaning |
318	+| -- | -- | -- |
319	+| No gaps | 0 | Every published version has a tag and a release. |
320	+| Gap | 1 | At least one version is published without a tag or a release. The step is red, also when release-plz was green. |
321	+| Could not check | 2 | An error or an unexpected response stopped a check. On a green release step, this is a `::warning::` and the step exits 0. On a red release step, the step stays red. |
322	+
323	+"Could not check" is never "no gaps". A network error, an API error, an empty package list and a `git_tag_name`, `git_tag_enable` or `git_release_enable` key in `release-plz.toml` all give "could not check". The report lists the reason for each item. To run the report locally, use `GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`.
324	+
325	+**Recovery.** The step summary shows the commands for each gap. In general form, with `<tag>` as `<package>-v<version>`:
326	+
327	+If the tag already exists and only the release is missing, skip steps 2 to 4.
328	+
329	+1. Give your `gh` token the `workflow` scope: `gh auth refresh -s workflow`.
330	+2. Look in the failed run log for the annotated tag object that release-plz made. Check it: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/tags/<tag-sha> --jq '{tag, sha: .object.sha}'`. The tag name and the object SHA must match the release commit.
331	+3. Create the ref: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs -f ref=refs/tags/<tag> -f sha=<tag-sha>`.
332	+4. If the call fails because the tag object does not exist, make a new annotated tag object at the release commit with `POST /git/tags`. Then repeat step 3 with its SHA.
333	+5. GitHub returns 404 for a draft release. Look for a draft with this tag in `gh release list`. If one exists, publish it with `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false`. Do not make a second release.
334	+6. Else create the release: `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag --latest=false --title <tag> --notes-file <file>`. Put the CHANGELOG section of that version in the file.
335	+7. Remove the extra scope: `gh auth refresh -r workflow`.
336	+8. Run the gap report again. It must say "no gaps".
337	+
338	+**Rule.** A red `release-plz` run can still have published crates. Do not assume that nothing shipped. Read the gap report first. Then check crates.io, the tags and the releases.
339	+
340	+**Rollout order for the SMA-745 change.** Run `sh scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` and set the three environment secrets before the merge. Merge only when no `release-plz` run is queued or in progress. After the first run on `main`, delete the three repository-level secrets. For a rollback, revert the workflow change. Restore the repository-level secrets before you do this.

604	+# SMA-745 — release-plz `POST /git/refs` 403 after a workflow-changing merge
605	+
606	+Linear: [SMA-745](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-745). Branch:
607	+`feature/sma-745-release-plz-post-gitrefs-returns-403-when-a-workflow`.
608	+
609	+## Intent
610	+
611	+A `release-plz` run must not leave a crate published on crates.io without its
612	+git tag and GitHub release. Sven said that the result to avoid is "a release that
613	+one must repair by hand". A larger permission for the paigasusbot App is
614	+acceptable to get this, but the extra risk that it brings must be contained in
615	+the same change.
616	+
617	+If a release still leaves a gap for a different cause, the `release-plz` run
618	+must report the gap and be red. Nobody must find it later by accident.
619	+
620	+## What happened
621	+
622	+On 2026-10-30, two `release-plz.yml` runs failed with `403 Forbidden` and an
623	+empty body on `POST /repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/refs`:
624	+
625	+| Run | Commit | Failed call | Effect |
626	+| -- | -- | -- | -- |
627	+| 41119756553 | `91a6ae65` (PR 314) | create branch `release-plz-2026-10-30T20-04-51Z` | none; the next run opened the release PR |
628	+| 41137079475 | `edc06f74` (PR 317) | create tag `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17` | evals 0.1.17 is on crates.io with **no tag and no GitHub release** |
629	+
630	+In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` (PR 315, PR 318) merged
631	+while the run was in progress.
632	+
633	+## Cause (tested on 2026-10-31)
634	+
635	+GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes
636	+on `main`, unless the token has the `workflow` permission. We tested this with
637	+Sven's `gh` OAuth token (scopes `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`; no `workflow`):
638	+
639	+| Target commit | Position | Result |
640	+| -- | -- | -- |
641	+| `edc06f74` | behind `main` by PR 318 (workflow change) | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
642	+| `b69fbf13` | tip of `main` | ref created (deleted again immediately) |
643	+
644	+The token, the ref name (`refs/heads/release-plz-sma745-repro`) and the call
645	+were the same. Only the commit was different. An OAuth token gets 404 and the App
646	+token got 403. Both are refusals of the same check.
647	+
648	+Not tested: that an App token **with** `workflows: write` succeeds. We cannot
649	+make an App token locally (the private key is only in Actions secrets). The
650	+first release-plz run with a workflow merge during the run is the first real
651	+evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
652	+
653	+Other facts checked:
654	+
655	+- The permission covers every ref write by release-plz: the tag ref in
656	+  `release`, and the branch create and force-update in `release-pr`. A GitHub
657	+  release on an existing tag, a tag object, and a commit made through the API
658	+  create no ref.
659	+- Token expiry (1 hour) is not a second cause. The longest of the last 30
660	+  release-plz runs took 12 minutes.
661	+- release-plz makes **annotated** tags (for example, the ref for
662	+  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.16` points to an object of type `tag`). It makes
663	+  the tag object first, then the ref. In run 41137079475 the tag object
664	+  `93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a` was made (tag
665	+  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17`, object `edc06f74…`, tagger
666	+  `paigasusbot[bot]`); only the ref failed.
667	+- `release-plz.toml` sets no `git_tag_name`, so the tag format is the default
668	+  `<package>-v<version>`.
669	+
670	+## Goals
671	+
672	+1. The paigasusbot installation token can create refs behind workflow changes.
673	+2. The extra power of that token cannot reach the release secrets from a
674	+   branch other than `main`.
675	+3. Each `release-plz` run checks for published versions without a tag or a
676	+   GitHub release, reports each gap with recovery commands, and is red when a
677	+   gap exists.
678	+4. The runbook describes this failure, the evidence, the report and the
679	+   recovery.
680	+5. `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 gets its tag and its GitHub release.
681	+
682	+## Non-goals
683	+
684	+- Automatic repair of a gap. The report only reports.
685	+- A change to the `concurrency` group. The runs did not overlap; it works.
686	+- Rules about the merge order of PRs, except during the rollout of this PR.
687	+- A check of older versions. Only the version at the run's commit is checked.
688	+
689	+## Anti-goals
690	+
691	+- A gap report that says "no gaps" when it could not check. A network error, an
692	+  API error, an empty package list or an unexpected response must show as
693	+  "could not check", never as success.
694	+- A report step that hides the original failure. The job stays red when
695	+  release-plz failed.
696	+- A gap report that gives wrong recovery commands because an auth or rate-limit
697	+  error looked like "missing".
698	+
699	+## Constraints
700	+

+## A red release-plz run with 403 on `git/refs` (SMA-745)
+
+**Symptom.** A `release-plz.yml` run fails with `403 Forbidden` and an empty body on `POST /repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs`. The failed call can create a release branch or a tag. On 2026-10-30, two runs failed this way. One run published `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 to crates.io and then failed to create the tag. The crate had no tag and no GitHub release.
+
+**Cause.** GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes on `main`. The token needs the `workflow` permission for this. In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` merged while the run was in progress. We tested this on 2026-10-31 with a token that had no `workflow` scope. The same call, ref name and token gave different results:
+
+| Target commit | Position | Result |
+| -- | -- | -- |
+| A commit behind a workflow change on `main` | behind `main` | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
+| The tip of `main` | tip of `main` | ref created |
+
+We measured only the 404 with the OAuth token. The App token got 403 in the incident runs. We think that both are refusals of the same check. We did **not** test that an App token with `workflows: write` succeeds, because the App private key exists only in Actions secrets. The first `release-plz` run that overlaps a workflow merge is the first real evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
+
+**Fix.** The `actions/create-github-app-token` step in `release-plz.yml` requests `permission-workflows: write`. The paigasusbot App (ID 3742291) has `Workflows: Read and write`. If the installation loses this permission, the token step fails. Then restore the permission in the App settings and accept it on the installation.
+
+**The `release` environment.** The extra power of the token has a risk. A leaked token can push a branch that has a new `on: push` workflow. Such a workflow can read repository secrets. The `release-plz` job therefore sets `environment: release`. This environment allows only the `main` branch. It has no required reviewers, so the release stays automatic. `scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` creates the environment. Set `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as **environment** secrets of `release`, by hand. Do not set them as repository secrets. A repository-level copy would be readable from any branch.
+
+**The gap report.** Each `release-plz` run ends with the step "report release gaps". It runs `scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`. For each publishable crate, it checks the version at the run commit. It reports a gap when crates.io lists the version but the tag `<package>-v<version>` or the non-draft GitHub release is missing. The script only reports. It does not repair. The step has three results:
+
+| Result | Exit code | Meaning |
+| -- | -- | -- |
+| No gaps | 0 | Every published version has a tag and a release. |
+| Gap | 1 | At least one version is published without a tag or a release. The step is red, also when release-plz was green. |
+| Could not check | 2 | An error or an unexpected response stopped a check. On a green release step, this is a `::warning::` and the step exits 0. On a red release step, the step stays red. |
+
+"Could not check" is never "no gaps". A network error, an API error, an empty package list and a `git_tag_name`, `git_tag_enable` or `git_release_enable` key in `release-plz.toml` all give "could not check". The report lists the reason for each item. To run the report locally, use `GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh`.
+
+**Recovery.** The step summary shows the commands for each gap. In general form, with `<tag>` as `<package>-v<version>`:
+
+If the tag already exists and only the release is missing, skip steps 2 to 4.
+
+1. Give your `gh` token the `workflow` scope: `gh auth refresh -s workflow`.
+2. Look in the failed run log for the annotated tag object that release-plz made. Check it: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/tags/<tag-sha> --jq '{tag, sha: .object.sha}'`. The tag name and the object SHA must match the release commit.
+3. Create the ref: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs -f ref=refs/tags/<tag> -f sha=<tag-sha>`.
+4. If the call fails because the tag object does not exist, make a new annotated tag object at the release commit with `POST /git/tags`. Then repeat step 3 with its SHA.
+5. GitHub returns 404 for a draft release. Look for a draft with this tag in `gh release list`. If one exists, publish it with `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false`. Do not make a second release.
+6. Else create the release: `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag --latest=false --title <tag> --notes-file <file>`. Put the CHANGELOG section of that version in the file.
+7. Remove the extra scope: `gh auth refresh -r workflow`.
+8. Run the gap report again. It must say "no gaps".
+
+**Rule.** A red `release-plz` run can still have published crates. Do not assume that nothing shipped. Read the gap report first. Then check crates.io, the tags and the releases.
+
+**Rollout order for the SMA-745 change.** Run `sh scripts/apply-repo-config.sh` and set the three environment secrets before the merge. Merge only when no `release-plz` run is queued or in progress. After the first run on `main`, delete the three repository-level secrets. For a rollback, revert the workflow change. Restore the repository-level secrets before you do this.

+# SMA-745 — release-plz `POST /git/refs` 403 after a workflow-changing merge
+
+Linear: [SMA-745](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-745). Branch:
+`feature/sma-745-release-plz-post-gitrefs-returns-403-when-a-workflow`.
+
+## Intent
+
+A `release-plz` run must not leave a crate published on crates.io without its
+git tag and GitHub release. Sven said that the result to avoid is "a release that
+one must repair by hand". A larger permission for the paigasusbot App is
+acceptable to get this, but the extra risk that it brings must be contained in
+the same change.
+
+If a release still leaves a gap for a different cause, the `release-plz` run
+must report the gap and be red. Nobody must find it later by accident.
+
+## What happened
+
+On 2026-10-30, two `release-plz.yml` runs failed with `403 Forbidden` and an
+empty body on `POST /repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/git/refs`:
+
+| Run | Commit | Failed call | Effect |
+| -- | -- | -- | -- |
+| 41119756553 | `91a6ae65` (PR 314) | create branch `release-plz-2026-10-30T20-04-51Z` | none; the next run opened the release PR |
+| 41137079475 | `edc06f74` (PR 317) | create tag `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17` | evals 0.1.17 is on crates.io with **no tag and no GitHub release** |
+
+In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` (PR 315, PR 318) merged
+while the run was in progress.
+
+## Cause (tested on 2026-10-31)
+
+GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes
+on `main`, unless the token has the `workflow` permission. We tested this with
+Sven's `gh` OAuth token (scopes `gist`, `read:org`, `repo`; no `workflow`):
+
+| Target commit | Position | Result |
+| -- | -- | -- |
+| `edc06f74` | behind `main` by PR 318 (workflow change) | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
+| `b69fbf13` | tip of `main` | ref created (deleted again immediately) |
+
+The token, the ref name (`refs/heads/release-plz-sma745-repro`) and the call
+were the same. Only the commit was different. An OAuth token gets 404 and the App
+token got 403. Both are refusals of the same check.
+
+Not tested: that an App token **with** `workflows: write` succeeds. We cannot
+make an App token locally (the private key is only in Actions secrets). The
+first release-plz run with a workflow merge during the run is the first real
+evidence. The gap report (below) catches a failure if the fix is not enough.
+
+Other facts checked:
+
+- The permission covers every ref write by release-plz: the tag ref in
+  `release`, and the branch create and force-update in `release-pr`. A GitHub
+  release on an existing tag, a tag object, and a commit made through the API
+  create no ref.
+- Token expiry (1 hour) is not a second cause. The longest of the last 30
+  release-plz runs took 12 minutes.
+- release-plz makes **annotated** tags (for example, the ref for
+  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.16` points to an object of type `tag`). It makes
+  the tag object first, then the ref. In run 41137079475 the tag object
+  `93f06c5ad30ce04fd74718430e28381531bb1b0a` was made (tag
+  `paigasus-helikon-evals-v0.1.17`, object `edc06f74…`, tagger
+  `paigasusbot[bot]`); only the ref failed.
+- `release-plz.toml` sets no `git_tag_name`, so the tag format is the default
+  `<package>-v<version>`.
+
+## Goals
+
+1. The paigasusbot installation token can create refs behind workflow changes.
+2. The extra power of that token cannot reach the release secrets from a
+   branch other than `main`.
+3. Each `release-plz` run checks for published versions without a tag or a
+   GitHub release, reports each gap with recovery commands, and is red when a
+   gap exists.
+4. The runbook describes this failure, the evidence, the report and the
+   recovery.
+5. `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 gets its tag and its GitHub release.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Automatic repair of a gap. The report only reports.
+- A change to the `concurrency` group. The runs did not overlap; it works.
+- Rules about the merge order of PRs, except during the rollout of this PR.
+- A check of older versions. Only the version at the run's commit is checked.
+
+## Anti-goals
+
+- A gap report that says "no gaps" when it could not check. A network error, an
+  API error, an empty package list or an unexpected response must show as
+  "could not check", never as success.
+- A report step that hides the original failure. The job stays red when
+  release-plz failed.
+- A gap report that gives wrong recovery commands because an auth or rate-limit
+  error looked like "missing".
+
+## Constraints
+
