    13	#   2. The tag <package>-v<version> exists (exact match).
    14	#   3. A GitHub release that is not a draft exists for that tag.
    15	#
    16	# Results and exit codes:
    17	#   0  no gaps.
    18	#   1  at least one gap (with or without "could not check" items).
    19	#   2  "could not check", no gap. When RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME is "success", the
    20	#      script writes a ::warning:: and exits 0 instead.
    21	# An error, an unexpected response or an empty package list is always "could
    22	# not check". It is never "no gaps", and never "missing".
    23	#
    24	# Environment inputs:
    25	#   GH_TOKEN               token for `gh` (read access to refs and releases).
    26	#   GITHUB_REPOSITORY      owner/name. Default: SMK1085/paigasus-helikon.
    27	#   RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA  path to `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1`
    28	#                          output. If unset, the script runs that command.
    29	#   RELEASE_GAPS_CONFIG    path to release-plz.toml. Default: <repo>/release-plz.toml.
    30	#   RELEASE_GAPS_SLEEP     seconds between crates.io requests. Default: 1.
    31	#   RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME   success, failure or cancelled. Unset means failure.
    32	#   GITHUB_SHA             commit for the recovery text. Default: HEAD.
    33	#   GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY    if set, the report is also appended to this file.
    34	#
    35	# Run locally: GH_TOKEN=REDACTED auth token) bash scripts/check-release-gaps.sh
    36	
    37	set -euo pipefail
    38	
    39	repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    40	repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-SMK1085/paigasus-helikon}"
    41	config="${RELEASE_GAPS_CONFIG:-${repo_root}/release-plz.toml}"
    42	pause="${RELEASE_GAPS_SLEEP:-1}"
    43	outcome="${RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME:-failure}"
    44	if [[ -n "${GITHUB_SHA:-}" ]]; then
    45	  sha="${GITHUB_SHA}"
    46	else
    47	  sha="$(git -C "${repo_root}" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo HEAD)"
    48	fi
    49	# crates.io refuses the default curl User-Agent with 403.
    50	user_agent="paigasus-helikon-release-gaps (https://github.com/${repo})"
    51	
    52	tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    53	trap 'rm -rf "${tmp}"' EXIT
    54	
    55	gaps="${tmp}/gaps.md"        # one block per gap, for the report.
    56	unknown="${tmp}/unknown.md"  # one line per "could not check" item.
    57	: > "${gaps}"
    58	: > "${unknown}"
    59	gap_count=0
    60	checked=0
    61	
    62	# Record an item that the script could not check.
    63	#   could_not_check <text>
    64	could_not_check() {
    65	  printf -- '- could not check: %s\n' "$1" >> "${unknown}"
    66	}
    67	
    68	# Print the report to stdout and to the job summary, then exit.
    69	finish() {
    70	  local report="${tmp}/report.md" unknown_count status
    71	  unknown_count="$(grep -c '^- ' "${unknown}" || true)"
    72	  {
    73	    echo "## Release gap report"
    74	    echo
    75	    echo "Repository \`${repo}\`, commit \`${sha}\`."
    76	    echo
    77	    if [[ "${gap_count}" == 0 && "${unknown_count}" == 0 ]]; then
    78	      echo "Result: no gaps. ${checked} published package version(s) checked."
    79	    fi
    80	    if [[ "${gap_count}" != 0 ]]; then
    81	      echo "### Gaps: ${gap_count} published version(s) without tag or release"
    82	      echo
    83	      echo "The recovery commands need a token with the \`workflow\` scope:"
    84	      echo "\`gh auth refresh -s workflow\`. Remove the scope after the recovery:"
    85	      echo "\`gh auth refresh -r workflow\`."
    86	      echo
    87	      cat "${gaps}"
    88	    fi
    89	    if [[ "${unknown_count}" != 0 ]]; then
    90	      echo "### Could not check: ${unknown_count} item(s)"
    91	      echo
    92	      echo "These items are not known to be correct. Do not read them as \"no gaps\"."
    93	      echo
    94	      cat "${unknown}"
    95	      echo
    96	    fi
    97	  } > "${report}"
    98	
    99	  cat "${report}"
   100	  # A failed write must not change the exit code: exit 1 means "gap".
   101	  if [[ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]]; then
   102	    if ! cat "${report}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}" 2>/dev/null; then
   103	      echo "::warning::cannot write job summary"
   104	    fi
   105	  fi
   106	
   107	  if [[ "${gap_count}" != 0 ]]; then
   108	    echo "::error::release gaps: ${gap_count} published version(s) without tag or release — see the job summary"
   109	    status=1
   110	  elif [[ "${unknown_count}" != 0 ]]; then
   111	    if [[ "${outcome}" == "success" ]]; then
   112	      echo "::warning::release gap report: could not check ${unknown_count} item(s) — see the job summary"
   113	      status=0
   114	    else
   115	      status=2
   116	    fi
   117	  else
   118	    status=0
   119	  fi
   120	  exit "${status}"
   121	}
   122	
   123	# Run `gh api --include <path>` with a time limit. Set `http_status` to the
   124	# status code from the first output line ("" if there is none), and write the
   125	# response body to the file `${tmp}/gh-body`. The gh exit code is ignored: gh
   126	# exits non-zero for every HTTP error, and only the status tells a 404 from an
   127	# auth error.
   128	#   gh_get <api-path>
   129	gh_get() {
   130	  local out="${tmp}/gh-out"
   131	  : > "${out}"
   132	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   133	    timeout 30 gh api --include "$1" > "${out}" 2>"${tmp}/gh-err" || true
   134	  else
   135	    gh api --include "$1" > "${out}" 2>"${tmp}/gh-err" || true
   136	  fi
   137	  tr -d '\r' < "${out}" > "${out}.lf"
   138	  http_status="$(head -n 1 "${out}.lf" | sed -n 's#^HTTP/[0-9.]* \([0-9][0-9][0-9]\).*$#\1#p')"
   139	  # The body starts after the first empty line.
   140	  awk 'body { print } !body && $0 == "" { body = 1 }' "${out}.lf" > "${tmp}/gh-body"
   141	}
   142	
   143	# --- tag format guard ----------------------------------------------------------
   144	# The script assumes the default tag format <package>-v<version>. It must not
   145	# guess another format, so a setting that changes tags or releases stops it.
   146	if [[ ! -r "${config}" ]]; then
   147	  could_not_check "cannot read \`${config}\`, so the tag format is not known."
   148	  finish
   149	fi
   150	for key in git_tag_name git_tag_enable git_release_enable; do
   151	  if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*${key}[[:space:]]*=" "${config}"; then
   152	    could_not_check "\`${config}\` sets \`${key}\`. This script knows only the default tag format \`<package>-v<version>\` with tags and releases enabled. Update the script for the new setting."
   153	  fi
   154	done
   155	if [[ -s "${unknown}" ]]; then
   156	  finish
   157	fi
   158	
   159	# --- package list ----------------------------------------------------------------
   160	metadata="${RELEASE_GAPS_METADATA:-}"
   161	if [[ -z "${metadata}" ]]; then
   162	  metadata="${tmp}/metadata.json"
   163	  if ! cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 \
   164	      --manifest-path "${repo_root}/Cargo.toml" > "${metadata}" 2>"${tmp}/cargo-err"; then
   165	    could_not_check "\`cargo metadata\` failed: $(head -c 300 "${tmp}/cargo-err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
   166	    finish
   167	  fi
   168	fi
   169	if [[ ! -r "${metadata}" ]]; then
   170	  could_not_check "cannot read the metadata file \`${metadata}\`."
   171	  finish
   172	fi
   173	packages="${tmp}/packages.tsv"
   174	# One line per package: name, version, crate directory relative to the
   175	# workspace root (absolute if it is not below the root).
   176	if ! jq -r '
   177	    .workspace_root as $root
   178	    | .packages[]
   179	    | select(.publish != [])
   180	    | (.manifest_path | sub("/Cargo\\.toml$"; "")) as $dir
   181	    | [ .name, .version,
   182	        (if ($dir | startswith($root + "/")) then $dir[($root | length) + 1:] else $dir end)
   183	      ]
   184	    | @tsv' "${metadata}" > "${packages}" 2>"${tmp}/jq-err"; then
   185	  could_not_check "cannot parse the metadata file \`${metadata}\`: $(head -c 300 "${tmp}/jq-err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
   186	  finish
   187	fi
   188	if [[ ! -s "${packages}" ]]; then
   189	  could_not_check "the metadata has no publishable packages (every package has \`publish = []\`), so nothing was checked."
   190	  finish
   191	fi
   192	
   193	# --- per package -----------------------------------------------------------------
   194	first_request=1
   195	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name version dir <&3; do
   196	  tag="${name}-v${version}"
   197	
   198	  # crates.io. Wait between requests (crawler policy: 1 request per second).
   199	  if [[ "${first_request}" == 0 ]]; then
   200	    sleep "${pause}"
   201	  fi
   202	  first_request=0
   203	  body="${tmp}/crate.json"
   204	  : > "${body}"
   205	  curl_rc=0
   206	  code="$(curl -sS --max-time 20 -A "${user_agent}" -o "${body}" -w '%{http_code}' \
   207	    "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/${name}" 2>"${tmp}/curl-err")" || curl_rc=$?
   208	  if [[ "${curl_rc}" != 0 ]]; then
   209	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the crates.io request failed (curl exit ${curl_rc}, HTTP ${code:-none}): $(head -c 200 "${tmp}/curl-err" | tr '\n' ' ')"
   210	    continue
   211	  fi
   212	  if [[ "${code}" != "200" ]]; then
   213	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io returned HTTP ${code} for the crate."
   214	    continue
   215	  fi
   216	  if ! listed="$(jq -r --arg v "${version}" '
   217	      if (.versions | type) == "array"
   218	      then ([.versions[].num] | index($v) != null)
   219	      else error("no versions list")
   220	      end' "${body}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
   221	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io returned HTTP 200, but the body has no readable versions list."
   222	    continue
   223	  fi
   224	  # A truncated list can omit the version and make a published version look
   225	  # unpublished. The list length must equal crate.num_versions.
   226	  counts="$(jq -r '"\(.versions | length) \(.crate.num_versions | if type == "number" then . else "missing" end)"' \
   227	    "${body}" 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown unknown")"
   228	  listed_count="${counts%% *}"
   229	  total_count="${counts##* }"
   230	  if [[ "${listed_count}" != "${total_count}" ]]; then
   231	    could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: crates.io lists ${listed_count} version(s), but crate.num_versions is ${total_count}. The versions list can be incomplete."
   232	    continue
   233	  fi
   234	  if [[ "${listed}" != "true" ]]; then
   235	    # Not published, so a missing tag or release is not a gap.
   236	    continue
   237	  fi
   238	  checked=$((checked + 1))
   239	
   240	  missing=""
   241	
   242	  # Tag. The singular "ref" endpoint matches the exact name only.
   243	  gh_get "repos/${repo}/git/ref/tags/${tag}"
   244	  case "${http_status}" in
   245	    200) ;;
   246	    404) missing="tag" ;;
   247	    "") could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the tag request for \`${tag}\` gave no HTTP status." ;;
   248	    *) could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the tag request for \`${tag}\` returned HTTP ${http_status}." ;;
   249	  esac
   250	
   251	  # Release.
   252	  gh_get "repos/${repo}/releases/tags/${tag}"
   253	  case "${http_status}" in
   254	    200)
   255	      draft="$(jq -r 'if (.draft | type) == "boolean" then .draft else error("no draft field") end' \
   256	        "${tmp}/gh-body" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
   257	      case "${draft}" in
   258	        false) ;;
   259	        true) missing="${missing:+${missing} }draft-release" ;;
   260	        *) could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the release request for \`${tag}\` returned HTTP 200, but the body has no readable \`draft\` field." ;;
   261	      esac
   262	      ;;
   263	    404) missing="${missing:+${missing} }release" ;;
   264	    "") could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the release request for \`${tag}\` gave no HTTP status." ;;
   265	    *) could_not_check "\`${name}\` ${version}: the release request for \`${tag}\` returned HTTP ${http_status}." ;;
   266	  esac
   267	
   268	  if [[ -z "${missing}" ]]; then
   269	    continue
   270	  fi
   271	  gap_count=$((gap_count + 1))
   272	
   273	  {
   274	    what=""
   275	    for item in ${missing}; do
   276	      case "${item}" in
   277	        tag) what="${what:+${what}, }tag \`${tag}\` is missing" ;;
   278	        release) what="${what:+${what}, }GitHub release \`${tag}\` is missing" ;;
   279	        draft-release) what="${what:+${what}, }GitHub release \`${tag}\` is a draft" ;;
   280	      esac
   281	    done
   282	    echo "#### \`${name}\` ${version}: ${what}"
   283	    echo
   284	    case " ${missing} " in
   285	      *" tag "*)
   286	        echo "Make the tag. release-plz makes the tag object before the ref, so first"
   287	        echo "look for the tag object SHA in the log of the failed run. If you find it,"
   288	        echo "skip the first command. Else make a new annotated tag object. \`${sha}\` is"
   289	        echo "the commit of this run: make sure that it is the commit that published"
   290	        echo "${name} ${version}."
   291	        echo
   292	        echo '```bash'
   293	        echo "gh api -X POST repos/${repo}/git/tags -f tag=${tag} -f message=${tag} -f object=${sha} -f type=commit --jq .sha"
   294	        echo "gh api -X POST repos/${repo}/git/refs -f ref=refs/tags/${tag} -f sha=<tag-object-sha>"
   295	        echo '```'
   296	        echo
   297	        ;;
   298	    esac
   299	    case " ${missing} " in
   300	      *" draft-release "*)
   301	        echo "Publish the draft release, or delete it and make it again with the command"
   302	        echo "below."
   303	        echo
   304	        ;;
   305	    esac
   306	    case " ${missing} " in
   307	      *" release "*|*" draft-release "*)
   308	        echo "Make the release. Use the ${version} section of \`${dir}/CHANGELOG.md\` as"
   309	        echo "the notes file. The tag must exist first. GitHub returns 404 for a draft"
   310	        echo "release, so first look for a draft with this tag in \`gh release list\`."
   311	        echo "If there is one, publish it with \`gh release edit ${tag} --draft=false\`."
   312	        echo "Do not make a second release."
   313	        echo
   314	        echo '```bash'
   315	        echo "gh release create ${tag} --verify-tag --latest=false --title ${tag} --notes-file <file with the ${version} section of ${dir}/CHANGELOG.md>"
   316	        echo '```'
   317	        echo
   318	        ;;
   319	    esac
   320	  } >> "${gaps}"
   321	done 3< "${packages}"
   322	
   323	finish

     5	# No pull request runs release-plz.yml. The gap report runs only on `main`, so
     6	# this self-test is the only check of the report before a merge. It runs the
     7	# script with fake `curl` and `gh` commands at the front of PATH and with
     8	# fixture metadata. It makes no network call and runs no cargo command.

    10	# Each fake answers from fixture files in a per-case directory (FAKE_DIR):
    11	#   - fake curl: FAKE_DIR/crates/<name>.status and <name>.body. A missing
    12	#     status file means "no response": the fake prints 000 and exits 28, as
    13	#     curl does on a time-out.

    15	#     the full `gh api --include` output. A missing file means no output.
    16	# Each fake writes every call to FAKE_DIR/calls.log. A call for the crate
    17	# `internal` (publish = []) writes FAKE_DIR/violations, and the case fails.
    18	#
    19	# Run: bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh

    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	
    23	repo_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

    26	tmp="$(mktemp -d)"

    34	cat > "${tmp}/bin/curl" <<'FAKE'
    35	#!/usr/bin/env bash

+# ---------- 5. Apply the release environment ----------
+#
+# The release-plz job uses `environment: release`. The environment holds the
+# release secrets, and its deployment branch policy allows only `main`. Thus a
+# workflow on a different branch cannot read the secrets.
+#
+# This section does not set the secrets. GitHub does not return secret values,
+# so this script cannot compare them. Set the secrets on the environment by
+# hand. See docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md.
+#
+# The PUT does not set `reviewers` or `wait_timer`. The release must stay
+# automatic.
+
+ENV_NAME="release"
+
+printf '%s\n' '{"deployment_branch_policy":{"protected_branches":false,"custom_branch_policies":true}}' > "$tmp_file"
+gh api -X PUT "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENV_NAME" --input "$tmp_file" >/dev/null
+
+POLICIES_JSON="$(gh api "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENV_NAME/deployment-branch-policies")"
+
+# Delete each branch policy that is not the `main` branch policy, so that a
+# re-run converges to exactly one policy.
+printf '%s' "$POLICIES_JSON" \
+    | jq -r '.branch_policies[] | select(.name != "main" or (.type // "branch") != "branch") | .id' \
+    | while read -r policy_id; do
+        [ -n "$policy_id" ] || continue
+        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENV_NAME/deployment-branch-policies/$policy_id" >/dev/null
+        printf '  %-30s deleted branch policy %s\n' "$ENV_NAME" "$policy_id"
+    done
+
+main_policy_count="$(printf '%s' "$POLICIES_JSON" \
+    | jq '[.branch_policies[] | select(.name == "main" and (.type // "branch") == "branch")] | length')"
+
+if [ "$main_policy_count" -eq 0 ]; then
+    gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/environments/$ENV_NAME/deployment-branch-policies" \
+        -f name=main -f type=branch >/dev/null
+    printf '  %-30s added branch policy main\n' "$ENV_NAME"
+else
+    printf '  %-30s branch policy main is present\n' "$ENV_NAME"
+fi
+
+echo "Applied $RULESET_COUNT rulesets, repo settings updated, environment '$ENV_NAME' updated."

# release-plz.toml — automated versioning, changelogs, GitHub releases.
# Reference: https://release-plz.dev/docs/config

[workspace]
# Bump dependent crates whenever a dep's version changes. The facade
# (paigasus-helikon) depends on every sibling via `[workspace.dependencies]`,
# so a `feat(core):` commit triggers: paigasus-helikon-core bumped →
# facade's `[workspace.dependencies].paigasus-helikon-core` line updated →
# facade itself gets a patch bump.
dependencies_update = true

# Force the scopeless release-PR title + commit (`chore: release`). release-plz's
# default SINGLE-crate template is `chore({package}): release {version}`, which uses
# the full package name (e.g. `paigasus-helikon`) as the Conventional-Commits scope —
# not in the convco/.versionrc + pr-title.yml allowlist (which uses short scopes like
# `facade`), so both the `commits` and `pr-title` gates reject it. The scopeless form
# matches the historical multi-crate release PRs and passes both. (Diagnosed on PR #58,
# the first facade-only release.)
pr_name = "chore: release"

# All library crates publish to crates.io (Stage 1 SMA-385 onward; the last
# stubs ascended in SMA-332/SMA-333). Remaining per-package overrides below
# are the only exceptions. See CLAUDE.md for the 4-step recipe a stub
# follows when it ascends.

[changelog]
sort_commits = "newest"

# Stubs: pre-published at 0.0.0 as name-claim placeholders. publish=false
# in each Cargo.toml keeps cargo from re-publishing them; release=false

I found no critical issue, and the branch can merge after two small fixes. The local self-test passes under bash 5.3 and under macOS bash 3.2. `shellcheck` reports no findings on all three scripts. `sh -n` on `apply-repo-config.sh` passes. The working tree stayed clean.

### Strengths
- The script reads HTTP status codes explicitly. It ignores the `gh` exit code. Every unknown result goes to "could not check". These rules meet the three anti-goals in spec §Anti-goals.
- The script uses the singular `git/ref/tags/<tag>` endpoint, which finds only the exact tag. The `longer-tag` self-test case proves this.
- The `num_versions` guard is an addition that the spec did not ask for. It prevents a truncated crates.io list from making a published version look "not published".
- The self-test checks what the output says, and also what it must not say (`!` patterns). It catches calls for the `internal` crate. It clears `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so that a CI run of the self-test does not write to the job summary.
- The workflow wiring agrees with spec §3:
  - The metadata step runs before the release step.
  - The `if:` covers the success, failure and cancelled outcomes.
  - The report step uses `github.token` and has `timeout-minutes: 5`.
- Security: `main-protection-checks` has no bypass actors. `main-protection-reviews` lets only the admin role bypass. Thus the App cannot push to `main`.
  - The `main`-only environment policy blocks the release secrets from other branches and from tags.
  - The three secrets are used only in `release-plz.yml`.
  - The pre-step and the report step get no secret.
  - I found no exposure wider than the spec accepted.
- release-plz side effects: the branch changes no file under `crates/`. The root `Cargo.toml` is a virtual manifest, and no crate sets `include` or `readme`. Thus this PR causes no version bump.
- CI for the PR:
  - The commit types are `docs` and `chore`. The scopes are `spec`, `plan`, `workflows`, `repo` and `release`. All five are in the `.versionrc` `scopeRegex`, and every subject starts in lowercase.
  - The `workflows` scope is in the `pr-title.yml` allowlist.
  - No gate runs actionlint, yamllint or shellcheck.
  - `docs/superpowers/**` is outside the markdownlint globs.
  - The new env keys do not match the cache-key prefix regex `^(CARGO|CC|CFLAGS|CXX|CMAKE|RUST)`.

### Issues
#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
1. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:226-227 — the fallback value turns off the truncation guard.**
   - **What:** if the second `jq` fails, `counts` becomes `"unknown unknown"`. Then `listed_count == total_count`, and the script skips the guard.
   - **Proof:** I ran `{"crate":"x","versions":[...]}` through the jq expression. jq exits 5 ("Cannot index string with string"), so the fallback runs.
   - **Why it matters:** an unexpected crates.io body can then make a published version look "not published". The script reports no gap and no "could not check". This breaks anti-goal 1.
   - **Fix:** use two different values, for example `|| echo "unreadable-list unreadable-count"`. Add a self-test case with `"crate":"x"` that expects exit 2.

2. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:311 and docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:66 — `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false` does not have `--latest=false`.**
   - **What:** when GitHub publishes a draft, it marks the release as "Latest" by default.
   - **Why it matters:** the "Latest" marker then moves to an old recovered release. Step 6 of the runbook and `gh release create` both use `--latest=false`, so the two recovery paths are not consistent.
   - **Fix:** add `--latest=false` in both places. The self-test pattern at selftest:290 still matches, because it is a substring match.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
3. **docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:73 and CONTRIBUTING.md (the release environment paragraph) — the runbook does not say how to check the environment secrets before the repository secrets are deleted.**
   - **Why it matters:** environment secrets override repository secrets only when they exist. If one environment secret is missing, the first run uses the repository copy without a warning. Then the deletion in rollout step 5 breaks the next release (a red token or publish step).
   - **Fix:** add one sentence: "Before you delete them, make sure that `gh secret list --env release` shows all three."
   - **Related fact:** if Sven does not run `apply-repo-config.sh` first, GitHub creates `release` automatically with no branch policy. The job still works with the repository secrets, so the run does not fail. Only the protection is missing until the script runs.

4. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:286-294 — the tag recovery text gives `object=${GITHUB_SHA}`, which is the commit of the run that found the gap.**
   - **Why it matters:** the report finds every gap that remains for a version, also a gap from an earlier run. On the first run after this merge, the evals 0.1.17 gap shows `object=<the SMA-745 merge commit>`. The correct commit is `edc06f74`, or the existing tag object `93f06c5a…`.
   - The text tells the reader to check the commit, so the risk is low. Sven also has the exact spec §7 commands.
   - **Fix (optional):** add the check command for an existing tag object from runbook step 2 (`gh api …/git/tags/<sha> --jq '{tag, sha: .object.sha}'`). Then the script and the runbook give the same steps.

5. **The evals 0.1.17 recovery is not done yet (Goal 5).** Until Sven does it, every release-plz run after the merge is red. A red run that is known to be red makes it harder to see the result of the permission fix.
   - **Recommendation:** do the spec §7 recovery before the merge. Then the first run after the merge gives a clean signal.

6. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:206-265, worst case against `timeout-minutes: 5`:**
   - Each crate can take up to 20 s (curl) plus 2 × 30 s (gh) plus 1 s (pause). With about 14 crates, a severe GitHub outage can exceed 5 minutes.
   - The step then times out red, with no summary. It never says "no gaps", so this agrees with the anti-goals. It only gives less information.
   - **Fix:** none needed. One sentence in the runbook could help.

### Deferred-minor triage
- `RELEASE_STEP_OUTCOME` other than success, failure or cancelled is read as failure, and no test covers it. **Can wait.** This is the safe direction, and the workflow `if:` sends only these three values.
- Recovery text has extras (`gh auth refresh -r workflow`, `--jq .sha`). **Can wait.** They do no harm and help the reader.
- check-release-gaps.sh:221-222 (now :226-227) and the `"unknown unknown"` fallback. **Must fix before merge.** It is an anti-goal-class bug with a one-line fix (Important #1).
- The append redirection at :195 (now :102) prints bash's own error before `2>/dev/null` applies. **Can wait.** It is noise only, and the exit code is correct (the self-test case `summary-unwritable` passes).
- The static guards are substring matches. **Can wait.** The brief asked for them in this form, and they still catch a removal.
- If the metadata pre-step fails, the release step is skipped and no report runs. **Can wait.** The run is red, and nothing was published.
- The policies list in `apply-repo-config.sh` has no `--paginate`, and the script does not say that a failure in section 5 leaves sections 1-4 applied. **Can wait.** There is only one policy, and a re-run converges.
- `gh release edit --draft=false` has no `--latest=false`. **Fix before merge.** It is a trivial fix, needed for consistency (Important #2). It is not a safety blocker.
- The claim "GitHub returns 404 for a draft release" has no source. **Can wait.** The claim is correct: the GitHub REST docs say that "Get a release by tag name" returns a *published* release only. A doc link is optional.
- release-ascend.md does not name the OAuth token in one sentence. **Can wait.** Line 42 already names it, so this is only a wording change.
- STE long sentences in ci-architecture.md. **Can wait.** This is style only.

### Declined to judge
- The use of the crate endpoint instead of the per-version endpoint `/api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>`. The spec chose the crate endpoint. I give it below only as a recommendation.
- The rule that a "could not check" result on a green run is a warning with exit 0. This is a spec decision (§3 table).
- Steps with `always()` that a job-level cancellation can stop. The spec accepts this.
- No check of older versions, no automatic repair, and no change to the `concurrency` group. These are spec non-goals.
- Whether `workflows: write` really fixes the 403. The spec says that nobody tested it, and I cannot test it in a read-only review.
- Repository secrets other than the three release secrets, and the bypass of the App on the `branch-names` ruleset. These are outside the spec's mitigation scope.
- Whether the environment `PUT` clears reviewers on an environment that already exists. The environment is new, and the spec wants no reviewers.
- A stale crates.io API response just after a publish. I have no evidence of it, and the report runs minutes after the publish.
- The content of the spec and plan files. They are design artifacts outside the markdownlint gate.
- A live run of `apply-repo-config.sh` or of any GitHub write API. The review was read-only.
- The runbook has a one-time rollout paragraph (release-ascend.md:73). This is a choice of where to put the text, not a problem of correctness.

### Recommendations
- Fix Important #1 and #2 before the merge. Each needs a one-line change plus one self-test case for #1.
- Add the `gh secret list --env release` check to the rollout text (Minor #3).
- Do the evals 0.1.17 recovery before the merge (Minor #5).
- Follow-up for a Linear issue: think about `GET /api/v1/crates/<name>/<version>` (200 or 404). It cannot be truncated and does not depend on the `versions` list. crates.io has said that this list can change.

### Assessment
**Ready to merge?** With fixes.
**Reasoning:** The design agrees with the spec, CI should pass, and no file in the branch causes a release-plz bump. The `"unknown unknown"` fallback is a small break of the anti-goal "could not check is never success". The draft recovery command also needs `--latest=false` so that it matches the other recovery commands. Both are one-line fixes.

I found no critical issue, and the branch can merge after two small fixes. The local self-test passes under bash 5.3 and under macOS bash 3.2. `shellcheck` reports no findings on all three scripts. `sh -n` on `apply-repo-config.sh` passes. The working tree stayed clean.

### Strengths
- The script reads HTTP status codes explicitly. It ignores the `gh` exit code. Every unknown result goes to "could not check". These rules meet the three anti-goals in spec §Anti-goals.
- The script uses the singular `git/ref/tags/<tag>` endpoint, which finds only the exact tag. The `longer-tag` self-test case proves this.
- The `num_versions` guard is an addition that the spec did not ask for. It prevents a truncated crates.io list from making a published version look "not published".
- The self-test checks what the output says, and also what it must not say (`!` patterns). It catches calls for the `internal` crate. It clears `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so that a CI run of the self-test does not write to the job summary.
- The workflow wiring agrees with spec §3:
  - The metadata step runs before the release step.
  - The `if:` covers the success, failure and cancelled outcomes.
  - The report step uses `github.token` and has `timeout-minutes: 5`.
- Security: `main-protection-checks` has no bypass actors. `main-protection-reviews` lets only the admin role bypass. Thus the App cannot push to `main`.
  - The `main`-only environment policy blocks the release secrets from other branches and from tags.
  - The three secrets are used only in `release-plz.yml`.
  - The pre-step and the report step get no secret.
  - I found no exposure wider than the spec accepted.
- release-plz side effects: the branch changes no file under `crates/`. The root `Cargo.toml` is a virtual manifest, and no crate sets `include` or `readme`. Thus this PR causes no version bump.
- CI for the PR:
  - The commit types are `docs` and `chore`. The scopes are `spec`, `plan`, `workflows`, `repo` and `release`. All five are in the `.versionrc` `scopeRegex`, and every subject starts in lowercase.
  - The `workflows` scope is in the `pr-title.yml` allowlist.
  - No gate runs actionlint, yamllint or shellcheck.
  - `docs/superpowers/**` is outside the markdownlint globs.
  - The new env keys do not match the cache-key prefix regex `^(CARGO|CC|CFLAGS|CXX|CMAKE|RUST)`.

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
1. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:226-227 — the fallback value turns off the truncation guard.**
   - **What:** if the second `jq` fails, `counts` becomes `"unknown unknown"`. Then `listed_count == total_count`, and the script skips the guard.
   - **Proof:** I ran `{"crate":"x","versions":[...]}` through the jq expression. jq exits 5 ("Cannot index string with string"), so the fallback runs.
   - **Why it matters:** an unexpected crates.io body can then make a published version look "not published". The script reports no gap and no "could not check". This breaks anti-goal 1.
   - **Fix:** use two different values, for example `|| echo "unreadable-list unreadable-count"`. Add a self-test case with `"crate":"x"` that expects exit 2.

2. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:311 and docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:66 — `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false` does not have `--latest=false`.**
   - **What:** when GitHub publishes a draft, it marks the release as "Latest" by default.
   - **Why it matters:** the "Latest" marker then moves to an old recovered release. Step 6 of the runbook and `gh release create` both use `--latest=false`, so the two recovery paths are not consistent.
   - **Fix:** add `--latest=false` in both places. The self-test pattern at selftest:290 still matches, because it is a substring match.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
3. **docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md:73 and CONTRIBUTING.md (the release environment paragraph) — the runbook does not say how to check the environment secrets before the repository secrets are deleted.**
   - **Why it matters:** environment secrets override repository secrets only when they exist. If one environment secret is missing, the first run uses the repository copy without a warning. Then the deletion in rollout step 5 breaks the next release (a red token or publish step).
   - **Fix:** add one sentence: "Before you delete them, make sure that `gh secret list --env release` shows all three."
   - **Related fact:** if Sven does not run `apply-repo-config.sh` first, GitHub creates `release` automatically with no branch policy. The job still works with the repository secrets, so the run does not fail. Only the protection is missing until the script runs.

4. **scripts/check-release-gaps.sh:286-294 — the tag recovery text gives `object=${GITHUB_SHA}`, which is the commit of the run that found the gap.**
   - **Why it matters:** the report finds every gap that remains for a version, also a gap from an earlier run. On the first run after this merge, the evals 0.1.17 gap shows `object=<the SMA-745 merge commit>`. The correct commit is `edc06f74`, or the existing tag object `93f06c5a…`.
   - The text tells the reader to check the commit, so the risk is low. Sven also has the exact spec §7 commands.
